current_example.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134367/assets/511f0d72f4758bcfc2bab8c5acac82163e9b75958a29758056ffc7a332d29371.svg)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134367/assets/3da4386e33c64fcb6538659665316030b1a37271ac2ca4ac06cf9fc5f93a627e.svg)

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134367/assets/0d142e17843c9de23045ba4d08a929b7df27af3781c094058ae79719565a032f.svg)

First, notice that since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134367/assets/5f31a4d4122fbb3aec9eca0cf2d3f2b2f08417acc06524c7ad5be99487284799.svg) 
 we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = e^y\cos x ,  
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} =e^y\sin x .
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\pi,0).$ This gives

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134367/assets/6df09a036d7cac0aa3b05ff601c7995e91c7213a202f847df051e7594ea90745.svg)
